producer_report.summary:
The steward is now a model-backed agent. Its stored prompt is unchanged, so it stays steward-1, and it is now the agent's system prompt. The run goes through the existing AgentDriver, so it is budgeted, hermetic and recorded. All checks pass: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked`. The one failing test (my own brief test, a helper missing a job id) was fixed and its steward tests re-run green. I did not rerun the full suite after that fix, or after the two last edits to steward.rs. Nothing was run against real Claude Code or a real `gh`.

**Root cause.** `steward::run` counted failure classes and never invoked a driver, so the prompt reached nothing. The fix is to wire the model call, not to edit the prompt.

**What changed**
- **Agent run.** `steward.rs` has an `Agent` trait and a `DriverAgent`. For each run it builds a read-only working directory: the code snapshot (owner private paths hidden), the records exported from HEAD, and `history/log.txt` (the last 300 commits with subjects and trailers).
- **Brief.** The agent gets a brief giving where to look, the ladder and which rungs Athena applies, the work item keys already queued, and the old failure count. `repeated_failures` is kept as input to that brief.
- **Background thread.** `AgentDriver::share()` is a new default method returning `None`; it is implemented for the real driver (a fresh `DeferredDriver`), `ClaudeCodeDriver` and `FakeAgentDriver` (cloned script). A driver that cannot be shared becomes a blind spot, never a model call on the main thread. A nested run still starts no steward.
- **Tool policy.** `Role::Steward` has no write access. `policy.rs` gains `check_gh` and `steward_commands()`. Allowed:
  - `git` `status`, `diff`, `log` and `show`.
  - `gh run list|view`.
  - `gh pr list|view|diff|checks|status`.
  - `gh api` with GET, no body, no `--hostname`, and no GraphQL.
  - Policy tests cover both the allowed and the denied cases.
- **Structured output.** `StewardOutput` has `work_items` (kind, key, title, rung, source, evidence, request) and `unread`.
- **Validation.** Athena rejects the whole output if an item has an empty key, title or request, has no evidence, cites a job not in the records, uses a path that escapes the repository, or uses a bad commit id. Free text is redacted. A rejected output becomes a blind spot naming `steward-agent`.
- **Queueing.** Each `unread` source becomes a `blind-spot:<source>` item. Every item goes through `decide()`, so rungs at or below the limit queue a request via `RequestQueue`, and higher rungs queue only a proposal. Keys already in the records, or earlier in the same run, are skipped before `decide` so they queue no second request.
- **Recording.** The invocation is a normal invocation record with role `steward`. It belongs to no job, so it is stored under `records/steward-runs/<month>/<run id>-01.json` and loaded into a new `Records.steward_runs`. No job's totals include it. A run with nothing to add, a recorded role and zero cost makes no commit; any spend is always recorded.
- **Also changed.**
  - A `finding` work item kind was added.
  - `invocation_record` became a free function (`build_invocation_record`) so the thread can use it.
  - Exhaustive `Role` matches were updated in the fake driver, scoring, the invariant check and three test files.
- **Docs and changelog.** `roles-and-ladder.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` say the steward now calls a model.
- **Tests.** `crates/athena-cli/tests/steward.rs` was rewritten with a scripted fake agent. It covers:
  - the fifth-task start;
  - ladder routing (one applied request, one proposal);
  - the blind spot from `unread`;
  - no double queueing;
  - spend recorded on a repeat run;
  - no commit on a free empty run;
  - an invalid output becoming a blind spot;
  - a nested run making no steward call.

  Unit tests cover `changes_from_output`, the brief and the steward schema.

**Judgment calls to check**
- The steward uses the verifier's model, cap and timeout, because there is no steward entry in `athena.toml` and that file is out of scope.
- The criterion that an empty run makes no commit conflicts with recording every invocation. I resolved it as above, so a zero-cost empty run leaves no record of itself in git.
- Git history is `history/log.txt` plus the working directory's single base commit, not the full object history. This keeps the owner's private paths hidden. `git show` of older commits therefore does not work, and the docs say so.

checks_run.note: All suites passed except my own brief unit test, which failed on a missing job id in its helper. I fixed it and re-ran only `cargo test --locked -p athena-core --lib steward`, which passed (8 tests). I did not rerun the full suite after that fix, or after the two last edits to steward.rs. `crates/athena-cli/tests/steward.rs` passed in the full run, and nothing it depends on was edited afterwards.
6 tests; the nested-run test failed on the first run and passed in the full run after I rewrote it

open_issues: No live test against real Claude Code and `gh`. The `--allowedTools` rules, the `gh` auth environment (the agent env allow-list may not pass GH_TOKEN) and the cost of a real steward run are untested; a missing `gh` or network is reported as a blind spot.
`docs/design/requirements-map.md` was not edited (outside the deliverables). Its A9-1 row still says the steward never calls a model; it should be updated, and stays Partial.
The steward uses the verifier's model, cap and timeout. A steward-specific `[models]` and `[budget]` entry needs an `athena.toml` change, which is out of scope.
The working directory has only a base commit, so older commits can't be inspected with `git show`; the log file and `gh` cover history.
A zero-cost empty run is not recorded in git, only mirrored in the state directory.
A failed agent run queues a single `blind-spot:steward-agent` item whose key then stops later failures being raised again. The error is also written to `steward-error.txt`.
mistakes: I first left a placeholder comment in `fake.rs` and a no-op `let _ = config` in `steward.rs`; I removed both before finishing.
I passed `--message-format=short` after `--` to clippy, which clippy rejected; I reran without it.
My first brief unit test used `JobRecords::default()`, which has no id; I set the id.
learnings: Invocation records must name a job and live under the job's directory, so the steward's records go to a new path, `records/steward-runs/`, loaded into `Records.steward_runs`, to stay out of any job's totals and invariants.
Athena has exhaustive `match spec.role` blocks in test helpers (`tests/common/mod.rs`, `run_pin_tests.rs`, `retry.rs`) and the fake driver, so a new `Role` needs an arm in each.
Snapshots never include `records/` and hide private paths, so the steward builds its own working directory: a Base snapshot, records exported from HEAD, and `history/log.txt`.
The producer's Bash policy has no grep, head or cat, and cargo's `--message-format` goes before the `--` separator or clippy rejects it.
In a nested run (`Athena.nested`), `go` lands the job even when the fixture deletes the README, so it cannot reuse the rejected-job helper.
desires: A way to run only a named test or list failures from `cargo test` without a pipe (the first full run's output was truncated).
A sample of real `gh` output, and the agent env allow-list, to check the read-only policy against actual commands.
